transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-22 15:00 PST | Duration: ~58m | Recording ID: ff-20260122-8742-qw-batch-budg
Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Park (Redwood), Aisha Khan (QuantumWorks, Head of ML), Tom Reyes (Eng Manager), Lena Park (Cloud Architect), Victor Han (SRE)

Summary: Quick scoping for a 4-week POC focused on unit economics and latency tradeoffs. Customer wants to validate per-token cost at scale with realistic batching/caching and two configs: hosted low-latency path and dedicated reserved cluster. Success criteria discussed: p50 latency targets, cost per 1M tokens, and cache hit improvements.

00:00 Marcus: All right hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick intro, i'm Marcus from Redwood and Priya is our SE, Jordan will be on the tech follow up.
00:12 Aisha: Hi thanks, appreciate it. We want to be very explicit about cost — our CFO is watching these numbers so this is a financial POC as much as technical.
00:22 Priya: Totally, that's the plan. Today we'll size workload, talk per token estimates, show how batching and prefix / KV cache knobs move the needle, and agree on success criteria and timeline.
00:35 Tom: High level, our traffic is mostly user-initiated chat and some async summarization jobs. Peak RPS is about 420 reqs/s, average tokens per request around 320 but with a long tail — some go to 2k tokens for long summaries.
00:50 Marcus: Good. A couple clarifying q's — is the 320 tokens counting both input+output?
00:54 Tom: yes combined.
:56 Priya: ok, that matters for token volume. Based on what you just said, rough daily token volume ballpark is 320 * 420 * 3600 * active_hours; i did quick math, if peak sustained for 6 hours that is ~2.8B tokens just during peak window — but we'll take sample traces to be precise.
01:10 Aisha: we'll send a 7-day anonymized trace after call.

01:18 Marcus: Benchmarks — we propose two baseline configurations for the POC: 1) Hosted low-latency config (pin to a faster model variant, small batching, streaming enabled) aiming for p50 under 200ms for generation only on short prompts; 2) Dedicated reserved cluster (higher batching, KV cache enabled, optimized kernels) aiming for better unit economics for sustained throughput.
01:40 Priya: Expected unit econ: ballpark hosted generation cost ~ $0.0025 per output token for the fastest variant we discussed, dedicated can get that down to ~ $0.0009–$0.0014 per token depending on batch sizing and quantization. these are fuzzy until we run with your traces.
01:58 Victor: That is a big spread, can you explain the levers?
02:03 Priya: Sure — primary levers are batching (continuous batching vs small immediate batches), KV/prefix caching which reduces repeated input tokens for multi-turn chat, model quantization (int8/int4) and kernel selection. For example, increasing avg batch from 8->32 can improve throughput and lower per-token compute cost by ~25–35% on our GPU profile.
02:21 Jordan: Also note that caching is workload-dependent: for conversational flows with reuse of system prompts and context you can see 20–45% fewer decoded tokens, but for one-off long summaries caching helps less.

02:33 Tom: Our budget constraint is pretty strict — CFO wants not to exceed $40k/month for inference for this workload in production. We need to figure out a POC config that proves we can meet both latency and that budget when scaled.
02:45 Marcus: Understood. Part of the POC is to produce a cost model: per 1M tokens, per-conversation, and at peak RPS. Priya will prepare a spreadsheet that takes your token trace and projects cost under different knobs.

03:00 Priya: For the POC runs we'll do three benchmark scenarios: baseline (no caching, minimal batching), optimized-latency (small batch, streaming on, pinned model), optimized-econ (large batch, KV cache warm, quantized model). We'll capture p50/p95 latencies, GPU utilization, tokens-in/tokens-saved, and unit $/1M tokens.
03:22 Aisha: What's a conservative estimate for tokens saved with KV cache? If we have multi-turn with repeated system content and references, i could see large savings but want numbers.
03:30 Priya: conservative: 12–18% saved; realistic for many chat flows 25–30%; in some highly templated flows up to 45%. We'll instrument with a prefix-hit metric and show delta across runs.

03:47 Lena: On infra questions: we will likely want the dedicated cluster in our cloud account (VPC) for the pilot if latency/throughput requires it. How does Redwood handle private deployment for this POC?
03:57 Jordan: For POC we can run a private sandbox in your VPC or a Redwood dedicated pool that we reserve for you. For private we need network whitelisting + service account + KMS key access if you'd like data never to leave the VPC. That's part of the security doc we'll send.
04:10 Lena: KMS is required; we also have to pass audit for ephemeral logs.

04:18 Marcus: Ok timeline: week 0 (this week) — exchange traces + finalize success criteria. Week 1 — baseline runs and warm-up; Week 2 — optimized-latency config; Week 3 — optimized-econ + quantization runs; Week 4 — analysis + final cost model and exec readout.
04:36 Tom: That sounds reasonable, CFO wants interim numbers by end of week 2.

04:44 Priya: Success criteria draft: (1) p50 latency < 200ms for conversational short-turns under hosted-low-latency scenario, (2) for sustained peak load the unit cost must be <= $0.0015 per token averaged across the day in the dedicated-optimized run to meet your $40k/month target, (3) caching should reduce effective tokens by at least 20% for the chat flows you flagged, and (4) no PII leakage — all logs masked in the replay. Are these OK to iterate?
05:10 Aisha: Agree, but add an availability target — we need 99.95% for inference calls during business hours.
05:17 Marcus: We'll add availability SLA as an acceptance criteria for the dedicated run.

05:24 Victor: For benchmarks, please include cost sensitivity to batch size. Our ops team is worried bigger batches will spike tail latency.
05:32 Priya: We'll capture p99 as well; typical trade is p50 improves and p99 can worsen if you wait for bigger batches — our continuous batching reduces that by thresholding latency SLOs. We'll show how to set batching max-wait and batch-size caps.

05:46 Tom: Any caveats on quantization? We care about quality regressions on long-form summarization.
05:51 Priya: We'll run quality evals on a held-out prompt set (you can flag which ones are most important). For int8 usually negligible diff, int4 sometimes needs a calibration pass. We'll include Rouge / embedding-similarity checks and a small human eval pass for highlights.
06:07 Aisha: Excellent. For the POC scope doc can you include an example cost calc?
06:12 Marcus: Yes — example: assume 1B tokens/month, dedicated optimized path yields $0.0011 per token => $1.1M /month (obviously that's a toy number), but for your actual traces we'll scale. For your $40k cap we need an average effective tokens/month ~36M at $0.0011 — we'll show exact math in the spreadsheet.
06:32 Jordan: We'll also show bucketed math: per 1M input+output tokens cost, and per-conversation average cost given your 320 tokens mean.

06:45 Marcus: On deliverables: we'll send a link to a Google Sheet template with sheets: raw-trace-ingest, baseline-run, optimized-latency, optimized-econ, quality-eval, executive-summary. Also security and deployment checklist doc.
06:58 Aisha: Please mark any assumptions clearly (e.g., reserved GPU pricing, quantization success).
07:05 Marcus: Will do. Any other questions?
07:10 Tom: Do we need custom kernels or is Redwood's runtime sufficient for our long sequences?
07:14 Priya: Redwood runtime handles long sequences; we may recommend a model variant with optimized attention kernels for >1k seqs. If there's a pathological pattern we can run a kernel-level test in week 2.
07:25 Lena: For the private VPC pilot we'll need an architecture diagram and network egress rules.
07:30 Marcus: We'll attach that in the security sync.
07:34 Aisha: Great — looking forward.

07:38 Marcus: Quick recap of next steps: Marcus + Priya send spreadsheet and security docs; QuantumWorks provides traces and confirms KMS constraints; schedule kickoff baseline next week. We'll aim for interim report end of week 2.
07:54 Call ends.

Notes: transcription includes some mis-hears (e.g., K V cache sometimes spelled out), occasional speaker attribution generic (Jordan sometimes labelled as Speaker 3 in the raw export).
